body:
Five small performance fixes for late-game 8v8 battles (~1,000 units, ~1,700 buildings, 16 players), from a read-only audit of `main` at bbbdac21. Tests come first: commit 3a0ec7e4 adds the GameTests alone. Its CI run (40439992066) shows `knockback_ignore_list_is_empty_after_a_tick_without_knockback` **failing on main** ("the knockback-ignore mark of a hit with no knockback was still there 2 ticks later"). The other five new tests pass on main, so they pin down the old behaviour. Each fix is its own commit after that.

Two measurement items from the audit were **dropped** because open PRs edit the same lines (see "Not in this PR").

## A. Night sources: one list per tick (`time/NightUtils.java`)
- **Finding:** `isInRangeOfNightSource` walked every building on each call. For each night source it rebuilt the centre from all of its blocks (`getCentrePos(getBlocks())`). A Mausoleum also worked out its range again from all buildings, three times per call. Then the method walked every unit's `NIGHT_WARPING` effect. It is called per undead unit for sun burn, per Spider for its sight range (fog, every 10 ticks) and from `Unit.tick`, on both client and server. The list it searches is usually empty.
- **Fix:** each side keeps one list of night sources: built night-source buildings (centre and range squared) and `NIGHT_WARPING` units (positions read live at each check). The list is rebuilt on the first check of each tick (Server/Client tick START marks it stale), and also right away when the building list or unit list changes size (on the server, also when the unit list's mod count changes). The blood-moon early return and the float distance maths are unchanged. The centre still comes from the building's current blocks. The stored `centrePos` is final from placement, and `setBlocks` can change the footprint on an in-place upgrade. Now this costs once per source per tick.
- **Behaviour note:** a source that turns on or off without a list change (a building finishing, an effect starting or ending) now counts from the next tick, not mid-tick.
- **Tests:** `night_warping_unit_still_covers_its_range` (in range; a far point unchanged; the night ends with the effect), `night_source_building_still_covers_its_range` (a built Stronghold, all within one tick).
- **Expected effect (estimate):** the cost of each call drops from O(buildings + units) to O(night sources). With ~200 undead/spider callers, that is roughly 0.5-2 ms per server tick, plus the same on the client.

## B. Knockback-ignore marks live one tick (`unit/UnitServerEvents.java`)
- **Finding:** `knockbackIgnoreIds` (an `ArrayList<Integer>`) got an id on every hit that must not knock back: every arrow, blaze fireball, wraith and so on. The id was removed only when a knockback event followed. Sometimes none follows: an arrow with no shooter, or a Ghast, Wraith or shielded Brute whose knockback an earlier branch cancels. Then the id stayed for the rest of the match, and every knockback paid an O(n) `removeIf` over the leaked list.
- **Fix:** an `IntOpenHashSet`, cleared at the end of every server tick. A hit and its knockback are one `hurt()` call stack (the damage event fires inside `actuallyHurt`, before vanilla's knockback in the same call), so clearing per tick keeps every real pair.
- **Tests:** `knockback_ignore_list_is_empty_after_a_tick_without_knockback` (red on main), `arrow_hit_still_ignores_knockback` (a real shot is still not knocked back, and its mark is consumed in the same tick).
- **Expected effect (estimate):** the leaked list grows by hundreds of ids a minute in archer-heavy fights. Each knockback was O(leak); now each is O(1) and the set is never bigger than one tick's hits.

## C. Minimap overlay buffer reused (`minimap/MinimapClientEvents.java`)
- **Finding:** every client tick allocated `mapColoursOverlays = new int[r*2][r*2]`: 480 arrays and about 0.9 MB at the large map (r = 240), roughly 18 MB/s of garbage.
- **Fix:** the buffer is zero-filled in place. It is reallocated only when the map size changed (`toggleMapSize` already reallocates). Every writer indexes inside it, and `MinimapViewQuadRenderer` draws into the array it is given, so the contents each tick are the same as a new array's. The full texture upload per tick and the metal-patch x building loop are left for a later PR.
- **Test:** none (no behaviour change; client-only).
- **Expected effect (estimate):** about 18 MB/s less young-gen allocation, so fewer and shorter GC pauses on the client.

## D. Item-pickup query skipped while no item exists (`unit/ItemPresence.java`, `unit/interfaces/Unit.java`)
- **Finding:** every unit ran `getEntitiesOfClass(ItemEntity, box)` every second tick: about 500 entity-section queries a tick at 1,000 units, although a match usually has no item on the ground.
- **Fix:** `ItemPresence.mayHaveItems(level)` gives one walk over the level's entities when its tick starts, and stops at the first item. Any `ItemEntity` that joins mid-tick (a drop, a death, a chunk load) flips the answer to "yes" at once. "No" is given only when no item existed at the start of the tick and none has joined since, so whenever an item exists the query runs exactly as before. A level not seen yet answers "yes".
- **Tests:** `item_dropped_after_quiet_ticks_is_still_picked_up`, plus the existing `worker_still_picks_up_an_item`.
- **Expected effect (estimate):** about 500 box queries per server tick removed in an item-free match, roughly 1-3 ms per tick at 1,000 units. In exchange there is one entity walk per tick that stops at the first item.

## E. Production-queue population once per owner per tick (`building/production/QueuePopulation.java`, `ProductionQueueList.java`)
- **Finding:** `getCurrentPopulation` cached its unit part per tick. The queue part still walked every building, with a string compare and a cost lookup per queued item, on every call. It is called per producing item per tick (`ProductionItem.tick` -> `isBelowPopulationSupply`), on the server and in the client's prediction (`UnitClientEvents`).
- **Fix:** `QueuePopulation` remembers the queue part per owner for one side's tick. The walk itself is the old loop, unchanged. It stays exact within a tick: production queues are now a `ProductionQueueList`, which bumps a shared atomic epoch on every change (add, remove, `removeIf`, clear, iterator and sub-list changes), and the building list's size is part of the key. So queuing several items in one tick, a finished item leaving its queue, or a building being placed or removed all count at once. Three things count from the next tick, as the unit part already does: a building changing owner, a graveyard's level, and a research that changes a unit's population cost.
- **Tests:** `population_counts_queued_production_as_before` (GameTest, one tick: queue three, remove one, clear, queue again, remove the building), `ProductionQueueListTest` (JUnit: every way to change a queue moves the epoch, and reading does not).
- **Expected effect (estimate):** from (producing items x buildings) to (owners x buildings) per tick. At 8v8 with ~150 busy labs, about 250k building visits per tick become about 27k: roughly 1-4 ms per server tick, plus the same in the client prediction.

## Not in this PR
- **M1 (UNIT_SHADOW in the eyes overlays scene)** and **M2 (a FrameParts section for the minimap's client tick):** dropped. #216 rewrites `EyesOverlaysScene.SECTIONS` (lines 64-71) and the `FrameParts` section table. #165 and #162 also change the `FrameParts` ids and names (lines 49-63). Any new section here would conflict with all three. Both are one line each once #216 lands.

## How to measure
- `/rts-perf 60` at minute 15+ of a bot match with 450+ units, on `main` and on this branch. Compare the `[Sys]` sections (`unit`, `buildings`, and the tick total plus "elsewhere", where `NightUtils` / `getCurrentPopulation` / the pickup query land today) and the `[PerfAuto]` heaviest entries.
- Client: the `[GC]` pause lines and `[FrameParts]` `minimap` while the large map is open.
- Shader shadow pass: eyes overlays scene 18 with shaders (UNIT_SHADOW is not in the scene's SECTIONS until M1 is done, so read `unitShadow` from the `[FrameParts]` line).

## Gates
- CI on 70c1dfb2 (run 40441399510): all green. That is `build`, `bar` plus the 8 `bar-tests` shards, and `bar-audit` (every test ran once). JUnit: 306 tests, 0 failed (the 3 new ones included).
- Flake stress of the six new GameTests, 10 runners (run 40442349243): `[Stress] 10 runners; 0 with any failure`. Each of the six tests passed 10 of 10.
- `check_java` on all tracked files, in batches of 400: 0 structural errors. The single-file run of `MinimapClientEvents` reports 2 "Component.x not public" errors, the same on clean `main` (a stub artefact).
- `tools/prepush.sh --quick`: everything passes except the two checks that also fail on clean `main` on this Windows machine (prepush's one-shot `check_java` call is longer than Windows allows; `anim_lab --motion` fails for all five anims on `main` too).
- No gameplay numbers changed. No file grows by 1,000+ lines. No client classes in the new server classes.

Do not merge without lovish's OK

Six GameTests written before the fixes, against the code they replace (lovish's
tests-first rule, design/LANES.md). The Oct 26 audit of a late-game 8v8 found
per-call world walks in NightUtils.isInRangeOfNightSource, a knockbackIgnoreIds
list that leaks ids, a per-unit item query every 2 ticks with no item in the
world, and a production-queue walk per producing item per tick in
getCurrentPopulation. These tests pin what a player sees:

- a NIGHT_WARPING unit and a built Stronghold still cover their night range,
  a point outside stays as it was, and the night ends when the source goes;
- a hit with no knockback after it leaves no knockback-ignore mark after a tick
  (FAILS on main: the id stays forever); an arrow hit's knockback is still
  cancelled in the same tick;
- an item dropped after quiet ticks is still picked up;
- queued production counts toward population exactly, inside one tick.
